title: Beyond the senses, the mind
theme: Beyond the senses is the mind, higher than the mind the sattva; above the sattva the great self, higher than the great the unmanifest.

words.context: Śaṅkara: the objects are included under the senses, «अर्थानामिहेन्द्रियसमानजातीयत्वादिन्द्रियग्रहणेनैव ग्रहणम्»

sandhi.type: m before a consonant; aḥ before a voiced consonant
sandhi.rule: Final m becomes anusvāra before a consonant, P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः); -aḥ becomes -o before a voiced consonant, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च).
Final m stays before a vowel and is joined to it.
A final t becomes d before a voiced sound, P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते).
A final n after a long vowel stays before a vowel and is joined to it.

sandhi.type: aḥ before a; m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: The visarga of -aḥ before a becomes u, giving o, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च), and the a merges into it, P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति); final m stays before a vowel and is joined to it.

morphology.note: uttama, a superlative in form (‘highest’), used here as a comparative with the ablative: ‘higher than’.
adhi with the ablative, ‘above’. Madhva’s text reads sattvād api, ‘even above the sattva’.
sattva stands here for the intellect (buddhi), as both Śaṅkara and Raṅgarāmānuja say, taking the place of buddhi in 1.3.10.

translation.literal: Beyond the senses [is] the mind; than the mind the sattva [is] higher; above the sattva the great self; than the great the unmanifest [is] higher.
translation.readable: Higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind the intellect; above the intellect the great self; and higher than the great self the unmanifest.

syntax: Four nominal clauses, each naming what is higher (param, uttamam, adhi with the ablative) than the one before; the series continues into 2.3.8.

ambiguities.note: The series repeats 1.3.10–11 with sattva for buddhi and without the objects (arthāḥ). Śaṅkara: the objects are included under the senses here, and the rest is as before, «पूर्ववदन्यत्». Raṅgarāmānuja: it restates the earlier teaching that, even with knowledge of the self as distinct from the body, refuge in the Lord is the means. Madhva: it is repeated to show that the great purport of all the Vedic statements is the Lord’s supremacy, known through the gradation of the deities.

beginner: This verse returns to a ladder we met at the end of the first chapter. Higher than the senses is the mind. Higher than the mind is the ‘sattva’, which the commentators say means the intellect, the power to decide and understand. Above the intellect is the ‘great self’, and higher still the ‘unmanifest’, the hidden source from which things unfold. The next verse completes the ladder. Śaṅkara says the steps lead inward, towards the inner self of all. Raṅgarāmānuja says the higher a thing is, the more it must be brought under control, and that the highest is reached by taking refuge in the Lord. Madhva says the ladder is repeated to teach that the Lord is above all. Why repeat it at all? Because the Kaṭha is building to its final teaching on yoga.
analogy: A ladder seen a second time from a different floor shows the same rungs in a new light.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Higher than the senses is the mind, higher than the mind the sattva; above the sattva the great self, higher than the great the unmanifest.

commentary.q: Śaṅkara: the inner self of all
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The self, of which the senses were said to be separate, is not to be sought outside, because it is the inner self of all, «यस्मात्प्रत्यगात्मा स सर्वस्य». The objects are included here under the senses, being of the same kind, «अर्थानामिहेन्द्रियसमानजातीयत्वादिन्द्रियग्रहणेनैव ग्रहणम्»; the rest is as before, and sattva means the intellect, «सत्त्वशब्दाद्बुद्धिरिहोच्यते».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Commenting on 2.3.7–2.3.8 together, he says the two mantras restate the earlier teaching of surrender: even with true knowledge of the self as distinct from the body, refuge in the Lord is the means, «देहविविक्तप्रत्यगात्मयाथात्म्यज्ञानेऽपि भगवच्छरणागतिरेव उपायः इति पूर्वोक्तं शरणवरणमेव प्रतिपादयति». ‘Senses’ includes the objects, as in 1.3.10, and sattva means the intellect, «सत्त्वशब्दो बुद्धिपरः». Being ‘higher’ means being harder to bring under control, «परत्वं च वशीकार्यतायां विवक्षितम्».

commentary.q: Madhva: the gradation that shows Hari supreme
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The series beginning ‘beyond the senses the mind’ is given again to make known that the great purport of all statements is the knowledge of the Lord as supreme, reached through knowing the gradation of the deities: «पुनः इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः इत्यादि देवतानां तारतम्यज्ञानपूर्वकं भगवतः सर्वोत्तमत्वज्ञान एव सर्ववाक्यानां महातात्पर्यमिति ज्ञापयितुम्».

commentary.q: The ladder of 1.3.10–11 and the Gītā
commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: The first adhyāya gave the same series with the objects and buddhi, «इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः». The Gītā has a shorter form, «इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः».

advaita.text: The series leads inward to the self that is the inner self of all, not to be sought outside: «यस्मात्प्रत्यगात्मा स सर्वस्य».

visistadvaita.text: Each stage is higher in being harder to control; the highest is brought under control only by refuge in the Lord: «परस्य च वशीकरणं शरणागतिरेव».

dvaita.text: The repeated series teaches the gradation of the deities, and through it the supremacy of the Lord, which is the great purport of all statements: «आधिक्ये सर्ववाक्यानां तात्पर्यं महदिष्यते».

schools.disagreement: The three read the same ladder to different ends: for Śaṅkara it leads inward to the self of all; for Raṅgarāmānuja each rung is a thing to be mastered, the last by surrender; for Madhva it is a gradation of presiding deities that shows Hari above all.

parallels.quote: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः
parallels.note: The first statement of the series, with the objects and buddhi.
The series continued to the puruṣa.

contemporary.text: Accounts of the mind often stack levels, from sensation to judgment to something deeper. The verse is an old version of that stacking. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: Which is harder to steer: your eyes, your mind or your judgment?
reflect.deeper: Why might a text repeat a teaching with small changes?
reflect.practice: Notice one sight today, then the thought it starts, then the decision that follows.

flags.note: Madhva’s text reads sattvād api for sattvād adhi (corrections.json).

Raṅgarāmānuja comments on 2.3.7–2.3.8 together (his mark ॥ ७,८ ॥); edition.json maps his 2.3.7 to that joint comment. madhva.json files his comment on the series under 2.3.6–2.3.8 (his mark ॥ ६-७ ॥, one off our numbering); it concerns 2.3.7–2.3.8.
The ladder as inward to the self of all (Śaṅkara), as degrees of what must be controlled, ending in surrender (Raṅgarāmānuja), or as a gradation of deities (Madhva).
